description: Gameplay camera (CameraRig) feel. The orientation and the per-map base framing come from the Blender export (sidecar cameras.gameplay: xform/forward, godot_size_keep_height); this file scales and smooths them. Every key has a reason under 'reasons'. Owner: the player/camera system (docs/runtime/PLAYER_AND_CAMERA.md).

reasons.ortho_size_scale: Iteration One framed each map's gameplay camera to show most of the map (16.9-28.1 m tall views, a 1.5 m character at 5-9% of the screen height). Play needs the character larger: 0.8x, clamped to the min/max below, keeps the character at roughly 7-11% of the view (classic MapleStory shows a ~70 px character in a 600 px window, ~11%).
reasons.min_ortho_size_m: Never zoom in so far that nearby monsters (spawn tiers are 10-20 m wide) leave the screen.
reasons.max_ortho_size_m: Caps the wide maps (Southperry, Field West of Amherst, A Split Road, Snail Hunting Ground III) so the character stays readable: at 19.5 m the 1.5 m character is ~7.7% of the view height (~70 px at 900 p). Checked in the sandbox screenshots; at 21 m Southperry's character read as small.
reasons.default_ortho_size_m: Used only when no sidecar camera is given (tests, empty scenes).
reasons.sidecar_reference_aspect: Blender's ortho_scale is the frame WIDTH at its 16:9 render (sidecar reference_aspect 1.77778; godot_size_keep_height = width x 9/16). MapSession hands the rig MapDefinition.ortho_size, which is that width (KEEP_WIDTH) x the map's ortho_size_scale; the rig divides by this aspect to get the equivalent KEEP_HEIGHT size before applying ortho_size_scale and the clamp, so set_bounds() and configure_from_sidecar() frame a map identically.
reasons.default_pitch_down_deg: Iteration One's fixed isometric pitch (every sidecar gameplay camera reports pitch_down_deg 40). Used only without a sidecar camera.
reasons.default_yaw_deg: Iteration One's fixed view direction: toward world +X+Y in Blender, i.e. Godot +X -Z (sidecar forward 0.5417, -0.6428, -0.5417); as a Godot camera yaw (rotation.y) that is -45 degrees. Used only without a sidecar camera.
reasons.distance_m: The orthographic camera sits this far behind its focus along the view axis, behind every piece of terrain, so the near plane never cuts through cliffs or buildings (no terrain clipping; occluders are faded instead).
reasons.near_m: Orthographic near plane; with distance_m it lies far in front of nothing.
reasons.far_m: Covers the island (x -68..351, z -84..779 m) and the sea from any focus.
reasons.dead_zone_fraction: MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 4.11: a dead zone of 0.15 x the view size (full box), so small movements and combat steps do not move the camera.
reasons.follow_rate_hz: Exponential follow rate once the player leaves the dead zone (63% of the gap closed in 1/7 s): smooth but never lagging far behind at walk speed.
reasons.height_follow_rate_hz: Vertical follow tracks the ground height (SafeGround / last floor), never the jump height, and eases over ~0.25 s so stairs and terraces do not jolt the view.
reasons.overscan_m: MAP_ARCHITECTURE section 4.11: the view may extend 6 m past the map's bounds to show island context, in the spirit of classic VR bounds.
reasons.occluders: Which exported meshes may fade (glTF extras category/group, OcclusionMath.is_occluder). The brief asks for trees, canopies, building roofs and tall props, and never ground or terrain: Trees and Architecture (walls, roofs, eaves, signs) always; Foliage, Props and the Vegetation/Props groups (giant mushrooms, hedge tunnels, hanging vines, lamp posts, forges, derricks, mushroom stems) only when their Blender instance (all parts of the unit, e.g. a giant mushroom's cap and stem) is at least tall_min_height_m, taller than the 1.5 m player, so flowers, bushes and crates never do (survey of all 62 chunks: Foliage averages 0.9 m). Never Terrain, Plinth (cliff skirts), Rocks, the island body or the sky, nor anything walkable (mushroom caps, roofs you stand on) or climbable (ropes and ladders sit right in front of a climber). room_groups / room_min_size_m: an Architecture mesh whose box holds a target's chest and whose ground footprint is at least room_min_size_m on both axes is the room it stands in and never fades for it (the interior shells and the Amherst cutaway house, 10-18 m; fading them would dither their floor and back wall around the player). 8 m separates them from the smaller architecture a player walks through or under (town gate 7.1 x 4 m, arches, trellises, the Southperry gazebo 5.7 m, signs, door frames, fence segments), which must fade like any building (review 2026-10-04: without the size the Amherst town gate's pillar and arch hid the player and never faded). A tree or hedge tunnel the player stands in still fades.
reasons.occluder_radius_m: Meshes whose ground footprint is within this distance of the player are tested each tick. At the 40 degree pitch a mesh h meters tall can cover the player from up to 1.19 h in front; the tallest occluders (15 m giant trees) need ~18 m.
reasons.occluder_player_half_width_m: Half the player model's on-screen width (the Player_Proxy is 0.89 m across with its arms): the body samples sit at the centre and both edges, so the whole silhouette is tested, not one ray.
reasons.occluder_hole_radius_m: Screen radius (meters on the view plane) around the player's chest inside which every occluder in front dithers out. 2.4 m is 1.6 body heights: the player and a monster touching it (spawn tiers, attack reach 1-2 m) read without a whole forest disappearing. The selection disc uses the same radius.
reasons.occluder_hole_edge: Soft rim of a hole as a fraction of its radius, so the cut does not end in a hard circle.
reasons.occluder_hole_depth_margin_m: A hole cuts only fragments nearer the camera than its target's centre plus this margin (half a body depth plus slack): the back of a canopy the player stands under, and anything behind the player, stay solid.
reasons.occluder_hole_floor_margin_m: A hole cuts nothing lower than its target's feet plus this margin, so the deck or floor a target stands on stays solid when the mesh carrying it is dithered (review 2026-10-04: the Southperry gazebo's one mesh holds the deck and the posts; its roof selected it and the cut opened a hole in the deck in front of the player). Costs the body nothing: at the 40 degree pitch an occluder point d meters nearer the camera covers the body on screen only if it is at least 0.84 d above the feet. 0.1 m clears the visual floor boards that sit 11 mm above the walkable slab (blender_export.md interiors).
reasons.occluder_dither_strength: Share of an occluder's pixels removed across a hole's soft rim at full fade (the core uses occluder_hole_core_strength). 0.9 leaves a sparse screen of dots around the player and the monsters so the tree still reads as present. Screen-door dithering is order independent: the old 0.7 alpha fade stacked a double-sided canopy's front faces, back faces and ink shell to ~90% opacity and hid the player (Snail Hunting Ground I report).
reasons.occluder_hole_core_strength: Share of an occluder's pixels removed inside a hole's core (where the cut is full, inside the soft rim), easing from occluder_dither_strength across the rim. #18: under the autumn canopies of The Field East of Amherst (000001020), with a monster in contact, the 0.9 dots alone covered 5-7% of the player's body pixels and 1-8% of the monster's; at 1.0 the bodies of the player and of every nearby monster show with no dots over them under any canopy, while the rim's dots keep the tree present.
reasons.occluder_monster_radius_m: Monsters within this distance of the player count as nearby: their bodies are occlusion targets too and get their own holes (the brief: "Can I see nearby enemies?"). 8 m covers the fight around the player in every view size (12-19.5 m tall).
reasons.occluder_monster_hole_margin_m: A monster's hole radius is half its sprite size (MonsterDef.sprite_size_m) plus this margin.
reasons.occluder_monster_default_height_m: Monster body height used only when the body on the monster layer has no MonsterDef (debug or test bodies); real monsters use their MonsterDef.sprite_size_m.
reasons.occluder_monster_default_width_m: Monster body width without a MonsterDef.
reasons.occluder_transparency: GeometryInstance3D.transparency of a faded mesh whose materials cannot be dithered (textured or transparent materials; none of the exported occluders today). Much further than the old 0.7, because alpha blending stacks layers.
reasons.occluder_fade_s: Fade in/out time, so occluders do not blink as the player walks past their edge.
reasons.xray_color: X-ray fill for the parts of the player hidden by terrain, props or the remaining dither dots (stencil test, drawn over everything): the player's shirt blue (Player_Proxy M_Flat_player_blue, sRGB #3B7AFF) at half opacity, so the hidden body reads as the player.
reasons.silhouette_color: See-through outline of the player, drawn on top of everything with the depth test off while anything hides the player: the player's own colour (M_Flat_player_blue, #3B7AFF), opaque.
reasons.silhouette_width_px: Outline width in screen pixels (the hull grows by width x view size / viewport height, so it is the same on a 12 m interior and a 19.5 m field).
reasons.silhouette_fade_s: The outline fades in and out over this time instead of popping as the player passes an occluder edge.
reasons.silhouette_terrain_heights_m: Heights above the feet of the physics rays toward the camera that detect terrain, cliffs and walls (which never fade) hiding the player and turn the outline on. They start at knee height so a step or root in front of the feet does not flicker it.
reasons.silhouette_terrain_ray_m: Length of those rays: past anything that can stand between the camera and the player (the tallest plinth skirts are 14.8 m; a ray rising at 40 degrees clears them within 25 m).
reasons.map_overrides: Per-map view size (KEEP_HEIGHT ortho_size_m, clamped to min/max) that replaces the scaled sidecar framing on that map, each with its own reason; empty when every map frames well with the global rule.
